tasks.short: Develop emergency plans covering recovery priorities, communications, critical processes and temporary shutdowns.

steps.what: Collect process inventories, contacts and existing plans from {DOCS}, {HCM} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Discuss disruption impacts, dependencies and minimum service needs with process owners.
Agree recovery priorities, shutdown triggers, decision rights and acceptable service compromises.
Write recovery procedures, communications templates and departmental shutdown instructions in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved recovery objectives, recovery strategy, verified baseline and plan template.
loop.output: Source-linked continuity plan draft with unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields and references; planner checks feasibility, dependencies and every operational instruction.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per section; unresolved facts return to process owners.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble fixed fields, but process-specific instructions require interpreting approved narrative evidence.

steps.what: Review the plan and approve organisational commitments and delegated emergency powers.
Publish the approved version in {DOCS} and distribute controlled copies through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A governed baseline in {DATA_PLATFORM} joins approved records from {DOCS}, {HCM} and {OPS_SYSTEM}; deterministic checks expose missing owners and inconsistent dependencies. A bounded drafting loop fills plan sections from approved evidence, while {WORKFLOW} routes decisions and publishes approved versions through {DOCS}, including controlled offline packs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources were fragmented, ownership was unclear and bespoke document assembly was costly. Recovery compromises still required agreement across departments.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing versioning and approval features cover publication. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, validation rules and document generators; bounded drafting handles narrative sections.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden dependencies, disputed recovery priorities and resource commitments remain difficult. A readable plan can still be operationally impossible.
tasks.human_edge: The planner exposes competing needs, challenges optimistic assumptions and secures commitments that hold during disruption.

ambition.what: Quarterly recovery-priority review after material process changes

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling documents and more time challenging recovery assumptions with process owners. Executives retain emergency powers and spending decisions; the planner can gain delegated authority to convene change-triggered reviews.

reach.task: Map cross-department dependencies and minimum viable services.
reach.learn: Process mapping, dependency analysis and evidence-based impact estimation.

evidence.claim: Continuity planning commonly combines records gathering, owner workshops, drafting and management approval; this decomposition is a model-based estimate.
Deterministic validation and source-grounded drafting are plausible components; the digest supplies no direct continuity-planning implementation case.
The digest documents a report containing invented sources, supporting explicit source validation for generated plans.

assumptions: Scope is one mid-size company with existing process owners and a designated executive sponsor.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
Estimates cover a first usable implementation using existing hosting and identity controls.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed data use.
unknowns: Completeness and ownership of process inventories and recovery objectives.
Available export interfaces and publication features in existing systems.
Delegated emergency powers and the approval route for shutdown decisions.
Employee data fields needed and applicable consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which plan defects are found most often during exercises?
Can dependency and document validation provide most of the benefit before adding drafting?
new_work: Review generated instructions against approved evidence.
Resolve missing owners and conflicting dependency records.
Maintain templates, connectors, access controls and distribution rules.
Check offline packs after each approved release.

tasks.short: Test disaster recovery plans, assess results and track corrective actions.

steps.what: Gather approved plans, recovery objectives and previous findings from {DOCS} and {PROJECT}.
Write exercise scenarios, test steps, evidence requirements and pass criteria in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved plans, unresolved findings, objectives and an exercise template.
loop.output: Scenario narrative and proposed test steps linked to approved objectives.
loop.check: Validate objective coverage and evidence fields; planner checks realism and separates simulated from live actions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported test steps go to the recovery lead.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed templates cover recurring checks, but scenario narratives require interpreting plan-specific dependencies.

steps.what: Approve exercise scope, live interventions, abort conditions and restoration responsibilities.
Arrange participants and test windows using {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}.
Execute approved recovery tests using backup infrastructure in {OTHER} and capture results.
Debrief participants and judge whether recovery outcomes meet operational needs.
Compile timings, evidence references and agreed findings into an exercise report in {DOCS}.
Agree corrective actions, owners, deadlines and retests in {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: An exercise workflow in {WORKFLOW} assembles approved plans from {DOCS}, prepares scenario drafts and coordinates test windows through {CALENDAR}. Structured evidence capture feeds deterministic comparisons and report generation, while approved corrective actions enter {PROJECT} with owners and retest dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exercise evidence arrived in inconsistent formats, and scheduling and report assembly crossed several teams. Live recovery tests required specialist control.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, scheduling rules and report templates already cover much of the paperwork. AI-assisted coding makes small evidence adapters more affordable, with bounded drafting for scenario text.
tasks.still_hard: Representative failure conditions, realistic workloads and safe test windows remain expensive. Passing a scripted test does not establish readiness for every disruption.
tasks.human_edge: The controller recognises misleading successes, pauses unsafe tests and draws candid lessons from participants.

ambition.what: Targeted retest decision after each critical corrective action closes

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time arranging exercises and compiling reports, and more time investigating weak recovery evidence. The controller retains live-test and abort authority; the planner can gain delegated authority to request scoped retests.

reach.task: Coordinate recovery test windows and corrective-action dependencies.
reach.learn: Change coordination, rollback planning and technical evidence acceptance.

evidence.claim: Recovery testing typically requires authorised scope, specialist execution, evidence review and corrective actions.
Scheduling, objective comparisons and structured report assembly can use deterministic automation; the digest supplies no direct recovery-testing case.

assumptions: The initial scope includes tabletop exercises and existing technical recovery procedures.
Build estimates cover coordination and evidence tooling, excluding new recovery infrastructure.
Time shares reflect a mixed exercise; technical tests and tabletop exercises will differ.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; consultation under national rules is assessed if participant recording or employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Existing backup infrastructure, test interfaces and approved runbooks.
Whether tests touch production services or third-party environments.
Available test windows, recovery specialists and evidence-retention requirements.
Whether employee participation or performance is recorded.
research_questions: Which recovery measures can be captured directly from existing test logs?
Which prior failures were missed by the existing pass criteria?
new_work: Review scenario drafts and maintain abort conditions.
Maintain evidence schemas and timestamp consistency.
Handle scheduling conflicts and missing evidence.
Validate corrective-action closure and decide when retesting is needed.

tasks.short: Develop recovery plans for physical sites containing critical assets.

steps.what: Gather site inventories, drawings, supplier commitments and recovery objectives from {DOCS}, {ERP} and {CLM}.
Inspect critical assets, access routes, utilities and alternate workspace arrangements on site.
Choose relocation options, restoration sequence and specialist support with facilities and technology owners.
Draft site recovery procedures, dependencies and escalation instructions in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Verified site records, approved strategy and specialist-approved procedures.
loop.output: Source-linked site plan draft with missing facts explicitly flagged.
loop.check: Validate assets, owners and dependencies; planner checks every instruction against approved technical procedures.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per section; missing technical instructions go to specialists.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields can be merged directly, but site-specific constraints and approved procedures require narrative synthesis.

steps.what: Validate technical sequencing, access arrangements and safety dependencies with qualified specialists.
Approve recovery commitments, expenditure limits and residual site risks.
Publish controlled site packs in {DOCS} and arrange restricted offline copies.

tasks.design: A site register in {WORKFLOW} links asset records, drawings and supplier commitments from {ERP}, {DOCS} and {CLM}, with deterministic checks for missing owners and conflicting recovery dependencies. A bounded drafting loop assembles site plans from verified evidence; specialist and sponsor approvals release controlled online and offline packs through {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site drawings, asset records and supplier obligations were maintained separately. Bespoke plan assembly was expensive, while physical verification could not be inferred from records.
tasks.enabler_now: Lightweight registers and document generators can be built more cheaply with AI-assisted coding. A bounded loop can organise approved narrative procedures without inventing technical instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Actual utility resilience, alternate-site capacity and supplier availability require verification. Specialist engineering review and physical improvements remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: Site specialists recognise physical constraints and unsafe assumptions that inventories and drawings miss.

ambition.what: Pre-move recovery-readiness assessment for proposed site changes

tasks.altitude: The planner spends more time inspecting weak dependencies with facilities and technology owners. They can gain a formal readiness-review role before site changes, while engineering acceptance and expenditure remain with accountable specialists and management.

reach.task: Assess utility dependencies and alternate workspace readiness.
reach.learn: Site inspection methods, asset criticality and limits of engineering competence.

evidence.claim: Site recovery planning requires physical verification and coordination between facilities, technology and operational owners.
Registers, dependency checks and controlled document assembly are feasible deterministic components; no direct site-recovery case appears in the digest.
The digest documents invented sources in a generated report, supporting source checks before technical plan approval.

assumptions: The first release covers one critical site with existing drawings and designated specialists.
Build estimates exclude engineering surveys, alternate-site procurement and physical remediation.
Site plans use specialist-approved technical procedures.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; employee consultation follows national rules where workplace or personal-data arrangements change.
unknowns: Number of sites, asset classes and quality of existing drawings.
Whether alternate locations and supplier recovery commitments have been tested.
Access restrictions on security-sensitive site information.
Required specialist approvals and applicable employee consultation.
research_questions: Which physical dependencies are missing from current asset records?
Which site changes should automatically trigger a readiness review?
new_work: Verify imported site records and resolve stale drawings.
Review drafted instructions with qualified specialists.
Maintain dependency checks and change-trigger rules.
Refresh restricted offline packs and supplier commitments.

tasks.short: Maintain and test emergency call trees, contact details and escalation routes.

steps.what: Export permitted employee contacts and reporting lines from {HCM}.
Ask contact owners to confirm numbers and availability through {EMAIL}.
Agree primary callers, deputies, coverage periods and escalation rules.
Update call-tree branches and telephone lists in {SPREADSHEET}.
Approve call-tree changes, drill recipients, timing, channels and test wording.
Start the drill by calling initial recipients and recording contact attempts.
Answer drill calls, acknowledge receipt and telephone assigned downstream contacts.
Reconcile acknowledgements, failed contacts and elapsed times in {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Permitted contacts from {HCM} feed a restricted register in {WORKFLOW}, where contact owners confirm details and deterministic rules generate call trees and flag coverage gaps. After a controller approves the exact drill specification, configured {TELEPHONY} notifications collect acknowledgements, apply approved escalation rules and feed a readiness report in {BI}; a controlled offline tree supports manual fallback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact changes and deputy assignments were copied between personnel records and local lists. Automated calling needed reliable acknowledgements, approved escalation rules and access to permitted numbers.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, notification services and scheduling rules can handle most steps. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of contact synchronisation and deterministic coverage checks; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: A delivered message does not prove understanding or availability. Shared telecommunications outages and out-of-hours coverage remain operational constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Managers agree workable coverage, respect personal circumstances and distinguish a missed acknowledgement from a real welfare concern.

ambition.what: Monthly decision on unresolved emergency communication coverage gaps

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time copying phone lists and chasing routine confirmations, and more time resolving uncovered roles and fallback weaknesses. They can gain delegated authority to run drills within an approved schedule; real incident activation remains with the designated incident lead.

reach.task: Maintain out-of-hours departmental coverage and deputy arrangements.
reach.learn: Coverage planning, escalation design and contact-data stewardship.

evidence.claim: Contact synchronisation, graph checks, scheduled notifications and acknowledgement reporting can use deterministic technology.
The supplied human-task prior overstates manual necessity for list maintenance and drill administration; acknowledgement and coverage judgements still require people.
The digest supplies no directly evidenced emergency call-tree product or implementation case.

assumptions: Existing communication facilities support approved test messages and delivery or acknowledgement records.
Only authorised contact fields are synchronised; contact owners verify personal numbers.
Automated drill dispatch uses the controller-approved recipients, timing, wording and escalation limits.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; personal contact use, out-of-hours arrangements and employee monitoring require assessment under national rules.
Consultation estimates allow for applicable employee representation; elapsed negotiation time may exceed working-day effort.
unknowns: Permitted use and retention of personal telephone numbers.
Existing acknowledgement, retry and escalation capabilities.
Applicable employee consultation and out-of-hours arrangements.
Fallback channels during a shared communications outage.
research_questions: Does the drill need to test human relay behaviour as well as direct reachability?
Which fallback channels remain usable during the disruption scenarios being planned for?
new_work: Resolve unconfirmed contacts and uncovered deputy roles.
Maintain escalation limits, test wording and approved drill schedules.
Review failures without turning drill participation into employee performance scoring.
Test fallback routes and refresh offline call trees.
Maintain contact retention rules and notification usage costs.

role.altitude: The continuity planner moves from document assembly and coordination toward validating recovery evidence, exposing dependencies and securing practical commitments. Any added authority concerns convening reviews and approved drills; emergency activation, engineering acceptance and risk acceptance remain explicitly delegated management decisions.
reach: Facilities managers: validate physical dependencies and alternate-site readiness.
Information technology project managers: coordinate recovery testing and corrective-action dependencies.
Management analysts: map minimum viable services and cross-department impacts.
Administrative services managers: resolve communication coverage and deputy arrangements.
skills_to_grow: Structured dependency modelling and data validation.
Exercise design and evidence-based recovery assessment.
Workflow configuration, access control and integration ownership.
Cross-functional negotiation and incident decision facilitation.
GDPR, EU AI Act applicability and consultation under national rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring recovery-readiness service that reviews planned operational changes, commissions targeted retests and presents unresolved recovery gaps for explicit management decisions.
